steps.message: The ask is time-related statics only, so I'll grep `StaticHeavy/` for `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` usage and ignore the file-system, console and network statics.

I scanned the whole `StaticHeavy/` project for time-related statics only. Found 7 time call sites across 2 `.cs` files.

### Time-related static call sites (7 total)

| File:line | Call | Note |
|-----------|------|------|
| Services/OrderProcessor.cs:21 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | order `CreatedAt` |
| Services/OrderProcessor.cs:22 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | order `ExpiresAt` (`.AddDays(30)`) |
| Services/OrderProcessor.cs:25 | `DateTime.Now` | receipt string |
| Services/OrderProcessor.cs:34 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | `IsExpired` comparison |
| Services/NotificationService.cs:7 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | days-until-expiry |
| Services/NotificationService.cs:16 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | log file name |
| Services/NotificationService.cs:18 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | log line timestamp |

**Count:** 7 occurrences — 6 × `DateTime.UtcNow`, 1 × `DateTime.Now`.

### Recommendation — TimeProvider

On .NET 8+ the built-in `TimeProvider` abstraction is the right replacement. Inject `TimeProvider` into `OrderProcessor` and `NotificationService`, replace every `DateTime.UtcNow` with `_timeProvider.GetUtcNow().UtcDateTime`, and pass `TimeProvider.System` in production. Tests then use `FakeTimeProvider` from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing` to control the clock deterministically.

### Migration plan

1. Add a `TimeProvider` constructor parameter to `OrderProcessor` (4 sites) — highest concentration, do it first.
2. Do the same for `NotificationService` (3 sites).
3. Update the DI registration to supply `TimeProvider.System`.
4. Add `FakeTimeProvider`-based tests for expiry and reminder logic.
